quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #3
										  					
  

30 Questions • Passing Score 24

questions.question: When changing lanes, what should you do?

options.text: Check your side mirror and look over your shoulder to make sure the lane is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your side mirror and look over your shoulder to make sure the lane is clear.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, check your side mirrors and look over your shoulder to be sure it is safe.

questions.question: Work zone barriers, drums, cones, and signs are used to:

options.text: Make drivers angry about slow traffic.
Keep traffic out of hazardous work zones.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep traffic out of hazardous work zones.
questions.explanation: Work zones are dangerous for workers and drivers. Watch for cones, barrels, signs, large vehicles, and workers in bright vests. They warn you and direct your traffic safely.

questions.question: A solid yellow arrow on a traffic signal means:

options.text: You should speed up so you can make the turn before the light changes.
You do not need to signal to turn from the indicated lane.
You should prepare to stop and yield to oncoming traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: You should prepare to stop and yield to oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: A solid yellow arrow means the green arrow protection is ending. Prepare to stop and let oncoming traffic pass before you turn.

questions.question: Before you enter an intersection, look to your:

options.text: Left, your right, then your left again.

questions.correctAnswerText: Left, your right, then your left again.
questions.explanation: Look left and right for vehicles and pedestrians. Look left a second time because vehicles from your left will reach you first. Check that the entire path through the intersection is clear.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: Wet roads are slippery and dangerous. This sign warns you to slow down because it takes longer to stop on wet pavement.

questions.question: If a traffic light is green but a police officer signals you to stop, you should:

options.text: Do what the vehicle in front of you does.

questions.explanation: Always obey a police officer's instructions, even if they contradict traffic signals, signs, or road markings.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: This sign means you cannot turn left. It is unsafe and illegal to turn left where this sign is posted.

questions.question: When another vehicle is passing you, you should:
questions.explanation: Keep your speed steady when being passed. Do not speed up. Let the other vehicle merge safely back into your lane.

questions.question: If you have had several beers, the effects will only be reduced by:
questions.explanation: Only time removes alcohol from your body. Coffee, exercise, or cold showers do not speed this up. It takes about one hour for your body to process one drink.

questions.question: The maximum posted speed limit should be driven only:
questions.explanation: The posted speed limit is the fastest you can legally drive under perfect conditions. Drive at the same speed as other traffic, up to the limit. All drivers must choose a safe speed at all times.

questions.question: How do you yield to an emergency vehicle?

options.text: Move to the right edge of the road and stop.
Speed up to clear the lane.
Move to the right lane and drive slowly until it passes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the right edge of the road and stop.
questions.explanation: Move as far right as possible when you see or hear an emergency vehicle. Stop and wait for it to pass. If you are in an intersection, drive through it first, then stop.

questions.question: Drowsiness affects driving the same way alcohol and drugs do. What does it do?
questions.explanation: Not sleeping enough causes poor driving. Like drugs and alcohol, sleepiness slows your reaction time, reduces awareness, and hurts your judgment.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Yellow signs with black markings warn of conditions ahead. This sign warns you that you are leaving a one-way highway and entering a two-way highway.

questions.question: When can you pass another vehicle?

options.text: When there is a solid line next to your lane.
When there is a broken line next to your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: When there is a broken line next to your lane.
questions.explanation: A broken line means drivers may cross it to change lanes. A solid line means you cannot pass. Only change lanes when it is safe.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Last turn before a toll road.

questions.explanation: Orange signs mark work zones. When you see orange signs, cones, or barrels, stay alert. This sign warns that a flagger is ahead. You must follow the flagger's directions.

questions.question: What is a dangerous habit in work zones?

options.text: Not watching for workers and equipment.

questions.explanation: In work zones, slow down and keep distance from other vehicles. Watch carefully for workers and machines.

questions.question: What color are traffic control devices in construction and work areas?
questions.explanation: Orange signs, cones, and barriers mark work zones. Use extra caution when you see them.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Orange diamond-shaped signs mark construction and maintenance areas. These signs help drivers and pedestrians stay safe. Fines for traffic violations may double in these areas.

questions.question: What type of sign is this?
questions.explanation: A triangle pointing downward is always a yield sign. You must be ready to slow down or stop.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Yellow signs with black markings warn of conditions ahead. This sign means a steep hill is coming. Slow down and shift to a lower gear to control your speed and protect your brakes.

questions.question: Fatigue increases the risk of:

options.text: Falling asleep behind the wheel and crashing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Falling asleep behind the wheel and crashing.
questions.explanation: When you are tired, you may fall asleep while driving and crash. Fatigue slows your thinking and increases crash risk. You or others could be injured or killed.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: This sign means you cannot make a U-turn. You cannot turn around to go the opposite direction at this location.

questions.question: You are driving on the freeway behind a large truck. You should drive:

options.text: Closer behind the truck than you would if following a passenger vehicle.
Farther behind the truck than you would if following a passenger vehicle.
To the right side of the truck and wait to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Farther behind the truck than you would if following a passenger vehicle.
questions.explanation: Follow farther behind a large truck. Large trucks have bigger blind spots where the driver cannot see you.

questions.question: Tailgating other drivers (driving too closely to their rear bumper):

options.text: Can frustrate other drivers and make them angry.
Cannot result in a traffic citation.
Reduces collisions by preventing being "cut off."

questions.correctAnswerText: Can frustrate other drivers and make them angry.
questions.explanation: Tailgating can make other drivers angry and lead to aggressive driving. You can receive a traffic citation for unsafe driving.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: A five-sided yellow or yellow-green sign warns of a school zone or school crossing.

questions.question: A sign with this shape means:
questions.explanation: A diamond-shaped yellow sign warns of danger ahead. Orange diamond signs warn of dangers near work areas.

questions.question: One vehicle that is required to stop at all railroad crossings is:
questions.explanation: School buses, transit buses, and vehicles carrying hazardous materials must stop at all railroad tracks before crossing. Be ready to stop when following these vehicles.

questions.question: What is the only medically proven method of removing alcohol or other drugs from your system?
questions.explanation: Cold showers, black coffee, and exercise do not reduce alcohol in your blood. The only way to lower your blood alcohol level is to wait.

questions.question: Collisions are more likely to happen when:

options.text: All vehicles are traveling at about the same speed.
One lane of traffic is traveling faster than the other lanes.
One vehicle is traveling faster or slower than the flow of traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: One vehicle is traveling faster or slower than the flow of traffic.
questions.explanation: Collisions happen more often when one vehicle moves faster or slower than other traffic. Driving faster than traffic increases crash risk. Driving slower than traffic also increases crash risk because other drivers may rear-end you or swerve to avoid you.

questions.question: Before changing lanes or attempting to pass another vehicle, you should:

options.text: Check your blind spots and mirrors.
Signal your intention before changing lanes.

questions.explanation: Always signal before changing lanes to alert other drivers. Check your mirrors and look over your shoulder to check your blind spot before moving left or right.
